Sasha — thanks for the materials and the clear timeline. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Ben (CS) to coordinate. Quick summary of Redwood's starting position so we can make this productive:
- Redwood generally accepts defend-and-control for third-party IP claims tied to the service, provided standard cooperation and notice provisions are met.
- We typically resist broad assignments of defense for outputs where the customer controls prompts and data; we can discuss a narrow assignment for specific use-cases (e.g., configured models delivered by Redwood).
- On defend-vs-reimburse: we can consider reimburse structures where there is an explicit carveout (customer prompt-derived infringement) or where insurance/escrow/indemnity cap mechanics are in place.

Suggested next steps:
1) Kimberly will propose specific redline language for: notice timeline (30 days for initial notice), selection of counsel process, and an evidence handoff checklist.
2) Ben will outline an operational evidence-staging plan (who on our side receives artifacts, expected formats, and secure upload path).
3) We should do a short call (30 min) early next week to align on the contested items and a narrow compromise path. Proposed slots: Tue 11/07 9:00-11:00 or Wed 11/08 13:00-15:00 PT.

I attach a one-page summary of our proposed concessions to speed review.

Attachments: redline_summary.pdf (pdf)

Hi Sasha / team — thanks for the redline and the evidence index. I did a first-pass legal review and have three core points plus a suggested compromise path:

1) Control of Defense / Selection of Counsel
- We can agree to "defend and control" for claims attributable to Redwood's service or model outputs where the model/response is produced without customer-provided prompt/content provably causing infringement.
- If EdgeWorks insists on an unconditional assignment of defense, Redwood needs: (i) an express duty to be notified promptly, (ii) the right to select defense counsel subject to reasonableness, and (iii) an ability to settle with an admission of non-infringement or without indemnifying EdgeWorks beyond settlement amounts.

2) Evidence / Notice SLA and Staging
- Proposed notice window: initial written notice within 30 days of becoming aware; an evidence staging folder with a defined manifest (see attached evidence checklist).
- Redwood operations will accept evidence via our secure SFTP bucket (instructions to be provided). Ben, can you confirm lead and retention window (we propose 90 days retention for staged evidence unless otherwise agreed).

3) Cap, Insurance Offset, and Reimburse Option
- We're open to a limited reimburse option where (a) the alleged infringement arises from customer-supplied prompts/data, or (b) the customer requests reimbursement for third-party claims where Redwood did not have a reasonable opportunity to defend.
- Cap: propose a contractual cap equal to 3x annual fees for the order form plus available insurance offset (policy limits). We will not accept an unlimited liability position.

Draft language is in the attached redline_comments.docx; key edits are inline and include a short cooperation checklist to be added to the order form. Timeframe: legal can finalize an internal position by 11/03 EOD if you can confirm the meeting slot.

Attachments: redline_comments.docx (docx)

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
